name: ApeCoin airdrop pays whoever holds a BAYC at claim time, flash-loanable from NFTX
summary: AirdropGrapesToken.claimTokens() pays 10,094 APE for every BAYC (and 2,042 per MAYC) the caller holds at call time and has not yet been claimed, reading balanceOf/tokenOfOwnerByIndex with no snapshot or holding period, so NFTs held for a single transaction count. In the first claim after the period opened, the attacker's contract took the attacker's BAYC #1060, flash-borrowed 5.2 vBAYC from the NFTX BAYC vault 0xea47b64e, redeemed BAYC 7594, 8214, 9915, 8167 and 4755, claimed 60,564 APE for six apes, minted all six back into the vault to repay the loan and sent the APE to the attacker; the vault, which cannot claim, kept its apes but lost their 50,470 APE allocation. Three blocks later another contract borrowed BAYC #731 from the NFT20 BAYC pool and claimed its 10,094 APE the same way.
notes: In the cohort as a code defect, by the same reading as other incidents that pay out on unsnapshotted current holdings (Beanstalk voting power, CRB2 dividends): the airdrop's payout depends on ownership the caller can borrow for one transaction. The NFTX and NFT20 pools' flash loans worked as designed and are not targets. The victims are those pools and their token holders, whose apes' allocations left the airdrop contract to the attackers.

Reset is startClaimablePeriod (0xb4fa6d55, block 14403934, refs), 73 blocks after the airdrop contract's deployment: it set claimStartTime, opened the 90-day window and unpaused the contract, which had been paused since its constructor. claimTokens could not run before it, so the first opening of claims resets the age (rule 8).

Anchor is the airdrop's first AirDrop event. Of the 16,534 claims to block 15100000, 97 claimants received and returned an NFT in the same transaction. Two drew on pooled vaults: the anchor (NFTX 0xea47b64e) and 0x29d3735e (by 0x95c2937f through 0x9eabb979, BAYC #731 from the NFT20 BAYC pair 0x7c155615, 10,094 APE), the campaign. The rest borrowed from ApeClaimBonusManager 0x32fbe88b (67, an opt-in BAKC rental service), BendDAO bNFTs for their own borrowers (all 0 APE), an Arcade AssetWrapper, or EOAs that had approved the claiming contract.

Loss counts the 50,470 APE of the anchor's five borrowed apes and the copycat's 10,094; the 10,094 APE for #1060, which the attacker bought on OpenSea for 106 ETH six blocks earlier (0x38e5465f) and owned before the transaction, was its own entitlement. APE had no market when it moved: these were the airdrop's first claims, and the first funded DEX pool was the anchor attacker's own Uniswap V2 APE/WETH pair (addLiquidityETH 0x9361aac5, 18 blocks later; the Uniswap V3 APE/WETH pool 0xac4b3dac existed but held no liquidity yet). Each claim is therefore valued at what its taker realised (rule 12): the anchor attacker got 392.56 ETH for the 44,600 APE it sold through that pool, its LP round trip and Uniswap V3 (0.0088019 ETH per APE; another 15,964 APE went to the unidentified 0x6a45f38b), the copycat 25.896 ETH for its 10,094 APE (0xd565b856); ETH at 2,800.78 USD. At CoinGecko's first quote half an hour later (10.36 USD) the 60,564 APE would be 627,443 USD.
